title: On-Prem SLA Exception & Maintenance Communications Runbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This file is a practical runbook for communicating SLA/SLO impacts and maintenance intentions to customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). It collects notice templates, escalation guidance, Terraform module notes for annotating maintenance behavior, and a lightweight upgrade plan checklist. Intended audience: Solutions engineering, Private Ops, Customer Success, and on-call SREs.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: planned maintenance windows, software upgrades, security patches, emergency hotfixes, and SLA exception communications for private customers (VPC + on-prem).
- Intent: provide clear, short, customer-facing messages and internal action steps so notices are consistent, timely, and contain the minimum required operational detail.
- Tone: transparent, operational, conciliatory when service interruptions occur; technical enough for platform owners but accessible for product teams.

Event classification (quick reference):
1) Routine planned maintenance: backward compatible, short reboot or service restart, <1 hour typical.
2) Version upgrade: model/runtime upgrade with staged rollouts / canaries. Estimated impact: variable; communicate potential SLO degradation.
3) Emergency/security patch: required immediately; may cause downtime during patch windows.
4) SLA exception: any event where SLOs/SLA credits may apply or where service levels fall below target.

Minimum timeline & notification rules (recommended):
- General planned maintenance: 14 days initial notice + 72-hour reminder + 24-hour reminder + 1 hour before start + completion notice.
- Low-risk patch (non-customer affecting): 72-hour notice + start/complete notices.
- Emergency patch: notify within 2 hours of decision, then follow-up within 24 hours with postmortem scheduling.
- SLA exception or extended outage: immediate outreach to primary contacts + daily status updates until resolved.

Audience segmentation (who gets which channel):
- Primary technical contact (customer): email + Slack (if integrated) + Jira ticket.
- Secondary business contact: email summary only.
- Platform/ops: dedicated Slack channel + PagerDuty if escalation needed.
- Exec stakeholders: only for multi-tenant incidents impacting committed SLAs.

Channels and cadence (recommended):
- Email: canonical record; include timeline, expected impact, rollback plan, and support link.
- Slack/Teams: operational updates, short bullets and status emojis.
- Jira ticket: canonical ticket for troubleshooting, attach logs.
- Status page / customer portal: update earliest available window for public-facing progress.

Templates (keeps short — fill placeholders):
1) Initial 14-day notice (planned maintenance)
Subject: Upcoming maintenance window for {{tenant_name}} — {{date}} (ETA {{duration}})
Body:
Hello {{tenant_name}} team,

We will be performing a planned maintenance window on {{date}} between {{start_time}} and {{end_time}} ({{timezone}}). Expected customer impact: {{impact_summary}} (e.g., short reconnections, brief 30–60s request errors, no data loss).

What we will do:
- {{short list of actions}}

If you have any must-not-exceed blackout windows please reply within 72 hours — we will attempt to accommodate.
Support contact: {{primary_contact}} (private-deployments@redwood.ai)
Best,
Redwood Private Ops

2) 24-hour reminder
Subject: Reminder: Maintenance for {{tenant_name}} tomorrow {{date}}
Body:
Quick reminder about maintenance scheduled at {{start_time}} ({{timezone}}). Expected impact: {{impact_summary}}. If this window is not workable, respond within 4 hours.

3) Start notice
Subject: Maintenance starting now — {{tenant_name}} ({{date}})
Body:
We have begun the maintenance window for {{tenant_name}}. We will post updates here and to your Jira ticket: {{jira_ticket}}. Estimated duration: {{duration}}.

4) Completion notice
Subject: Maintenance complete — {{tenant_name}} ({{date}})
Body:
Maintenance finished at {{time}}. Observed outcome: {{outcome_summary}}. If you see any regressions, please re-open {{jira_ticket}} or reply to this message.

5) SLA exception initial outreach (urgent)
Subject: SLA Exception declared for {{tenant_name}} — incident {{incident_id}}
Body:
We detected a service condition that may affect SLA commitments for {{tenant_name}}. We've opened incident {{incident_id}} ({{jira_ticket}}). Immediate steps we are taking:
- Triage owner: {{owner_name}}
- Estimated time to resolution: TBD
We will provide hourly updates until resolution. A postmortem will be scheduled within 3 business days.

Internal checklist for any notice (pre-send):
- Confirm window with infra calendar and customer blackout list.
- Verify backup/snapshot status and retention (DB, disk images).
- Confirm rollback plan and at least one verified rollback step.
- Update internal Slack ops channel and attach Jira ticket link.
- Verify Terraform module annotations (see Terraform notes).

Terraform module notes (practical guidance):
- Goal: allow the platform code and oncall tooling to compute tenant maintenance windows and to tag resources for maintenance-aware scheduling.
- Minimal recommended variables on tenant module:
  - maintenance_window: string (cron-like or RFC3339 range)
  - maintenance_owner: string (email/ID)
  - maintenance_exempt: bool (true if no automated forced upgrades)
- Resource tagging pattern (strings):
  - tag: "rw:maintenance_owner={{email}}"
  - tag: "rw:maintenance_window={{cron}}"
- Example (pseudo-terraform snippet):
  # attach tags to the VM / VMSS / instance group
  resource "aws_instance" "app" {
    # ...
    tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
      "rw:tenant_id" = var.tenant_id,
      "rw:maintenance_owner" = var.maintenance_owner,
      "rw:maintenance_window" = var.maintenance_window,
    })
  }
- Module contract note: do not hardcode timezones; store windows in UTC and let the notification system translate.
- Recommendation: add a lifecycle hook "pre-upgrade-snapshot" that triggers an infra snapshot and records the snapshot id in terraform outputs for auditing.

Upgrade plan checklist (lightweight, meant to be copied into ticket):
Pre-upgrade (72h)
- Confirm customer acceptance window and blackout constraints.
- Validate backups and snapshots completed; list snapshot ids.
- Smoke test baseline: capture synthetic request traces and latency percentiles.
- Ensure canary nodes / subset of traffic and staging environment prepared.
- Security review signoff for package patches.

During upgrade
- Put non-critical clients into degraded routing if supported.
- Run canary on 5% of instances for 15–30 minutes. Collect logs and metrics.
- Progressively move to 25% then 100% if no regressions.
- Keep rollback button clearly documented and tested.

Post-upgrade verification (0–6h)
- Run acceptance suites: healthchecks, 95/99 p50/p95 latency checks.
- Verify KV cache integrity and model latency profiles.
- Notify customer with observed metrics and whether SLOs met.

Rollback / emergency rollback steps
- Trigger automation to redeploy previous AMI/container image or restore from snapshot.
- If database schema changed, run pre-authorized downgrade path only if safe — otherwise contact engineering lead.

SLO statement for notices (short):
- "During this window we may not meet our SLO for 95th percentile tail latency. We estimate any user-facing errors will be <= X% and limited to short retries; we will report final metrics after the maintenance completes."

Escalation matrix (template)
- Level 1: oncall-private-ops (pager) — 1st responder (15 min)
- Level 2: SRE lead (30 min)
- Level 3: Engineering manager + Solutions Eng (60 min)
- Level 4: VP Eng + CS lead (if SLA credit likely)

Operational artifacts to collect for postmortem:
- Timestamped logs (start → end) from app/ingress/control plane.
- APM traces for affected requests.
- Terraform plan/apply logs and module outputs.
- Snapshot ids and storage checksums.
- Customer-visible error rates and latencies (pre/post).

Postmortem template (bullet starter):
- Incident summary: what happened, who/when declared SLA exception.
- Timeline: minute-granular events.
- Root cause analysis: immediate and underlying causes.
- Mitigation and rollback steps taken.
- Customer impact summary and proposed SLA remediation (credits or other).
- Action items and owners with due dates (create follow-up Jira).

Open TODOs / discussion points (internal):
- Add an automation hook in terraform-module to emit a maintenance-ready boolean to the control plane.
- Standardize tenant tag names across cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure).
- Decide default notification windows for high-frequency patching customers.

Appendix: quick examples and placeholders (copy/paste)
- Slack status update during event:
  "MAINTENCE STARTING: {{tenant_name}} - maintenance began at {{time}} UTC. ETA {{duration}}. Jira: {{jira_ticket}}. Owner: {{owner}}"

- Simple terraform variable block example (to paste into tenant module):
  variable "maintenance_window" {
    type = string
    description = "UTC maintenance window: e.g. 2026-03-10T23:00:00Z/2026-03-11T01:00:00Z or cron:0 2 * * 1"
  }

Notes and provenance:
- This file is a working draft used by eng-private-deployments and solutions-eng for private customer upgrades. Use it as a basis; replace placeholders with tenant-specific values.
- Expected next steps: review with CS and SRE, add automation tasks to terraform modules PR, and land a template into the customer portal.

Last reviewed by: Marcus Liu on 2026-02-28
